subject: Private offer — geo tax passback + partner margin treatment
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@helix.ai>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helix.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private offer: regional tax passthrough + partner margin question

Hi David —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement looped me in to lock down economics for a private offer we want to submit in Azure Marketplace for EU territories. Two quick asks so we can move the PO to legal: 

1) Tax passthrough: we have a requirement to show VAT treatment separately on the marketplace invoice. Can the private offer reflect a tax line that mirrors local VAT (we'll provide the country-level tax matrix)? If not, what are the recommended evidence docs/process for our tax team?

2) Channel margin / passback: Helix expects a 10% reseller uplift to accommodate our local partner network. The marketplace private offer flow shows a single committed price. Do you have a standard way to signal/reserve a channel margin (passback) while keeping the committed list price? We need to present something to our partners for contract alignment.

I attached our tax matrix and an initial PO draft. Can you confirm whether the marketplace private offer can carry separate tax lines and whether Redwood has a recommended passback mechanism (list of supported options would be ideal)?

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement — Helix.ai
liam.oconnor@helix.ai

Attachments: Helix_tax_matrix_Q2.pdf, HLX_PO_draft_4857.docx

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@helix.ai>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private offer: regional tax passthrough + partner margin question

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sending the matrix. Short answers up front: yes on invoices showing tax lines (with constraints) and yes on supporting partner passback workflows — but both have a few operational caveats. High-level: 

- Tax lines: We can enable VAT as a separate line on the invoice for Azure private offers, provided the customer/marketplace billing settings map country -> tax rate. For EU multi-country POs we usually require a per-country billing address or tax mapping during procurement intake to ensure the marketplace issues the correct VAT. We will need the country-level rates from your matrix mapped to the final list of billing jurisdictions.

- Channel passback: We support a pair of patterns — (A) explicit partner rebate passback via invoice routing (Redwood issues net revenue to partner and Helix reconciles invoice credits), or (B) reserved channel uplift accounted outside the marketplace as a shadow rebate (Helix pays full list price, Redwood issues a post-invoice credit). Pattern A is cleaner for bookkeeping but requires that the partner be registered in Azure/Reseller program and listed on the PO. Pattern B is faster but creates an off-invoice settlement.

I'll loop in Irene (tax/compliance) for the VAT operational steps and Jordan (marketplace ops) for the passback implementation details. Can you confirm the list of EU countries the PO will cover and whether the partner is already onboarded in Azure as an authorized reseller?

Next steps: Irene will advise required evidence and mapping; Jordan will outline the passback options with expected time-to-live and required docs. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement/legal through both flows.

Thanks,
David
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
--
redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private offer: regional tax passthrough + partner margin question

Hi Liam / team —

Thanks, David. A few operational notes from a compliance/tax perspective: 

1) Evidence we need to map VAT per invoice: billing address list (country-level), company VAT registration numbers for each billing entity, and the final PO line items with regional allocation. Without per-country billing addresses we cannot reliably split VAT on a single marketplace invoice.

2) If Helix wants Redwood to surface the tax line on the Azure invoice, we'll request confirmation that Helix's marketplace account will accept tax-exempt/reseller flows where applicable. For some EU territories there are reverse-charge scenarios — we will need Helix's legal confirmation for each jurisdiction.

3) Timeline: If procurement provides the country list and VAT numbers by end of day Friday (local time), we can configure per-country tax mapping in the private-offer provisioning flow and generate a test invoice within 3 business days.

I added Vanessa from Partner Operations to help with onboarding/reseller verification (if you want pattern A). Vanessa, please advise on required partner docs and onboarding ETA.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Hi all —

Thanks for the fast response. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Countries: Germany, France, Spain, Netherlands, Ireland. We'll provide VAT registration numbers for each country by COB today (14 Jun CET).
- Partner status: Our regional partner (DataBridge Ltd) is not yet listed in Azure as an authorized reseller — we expect them to be onboarded in two weeks. We prefer Pattern A (explicit passback) but we can accept Pattern B if Pattern A would delay the PO materially.

1) Can you confirm whether Pattern A requires DataBridge to be fully onboarded before the private offer is committed, or whether they can be registered during the provisioning window?
2) If Pattern B is used as interim, what does the reconciliation cadence look like (monthly, quarterly)? Any sample workback docs would help our finance team.

I attached the VAT matrix and PO again. Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow morning UK time if that helps.

Regards,
Liam

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private offer: regional tax passthrough + partner margin question

Hi Liam —

Quick operational reply on the passback options so you can share with your finance/legal: 

Pattern A (preferred):
- Requires partner (DataBridge Ltd) to be registered in Azure and attached to the private-offer during provisioning. You can start the PO commit while onboarding is in progress, but the partner needs to be active before the first invoice run that includes the passback routing. Typical onboarding + verification is 7-12 business days.
- Mechanism: Marketplace private offer can route a portion of invoiced revenue to a partner via reseller mapping (we mark the partner in the offer metadata). The partner receives their share through Azure settlement; Redwood issues a net revenue report for reconciliation.

Pattern B (interim):
- No partner onboarding required at time of commit. Redwood invoices Helix for the full committed price; Redwood issues a separate partner rebate credit (post-invoice) to Helix which Helix then routes to DataBridge.
- Reconciliation cadence: monthly statements and netting, with a 30-day payment window after statement issue. We provide a template reconciliation workbook (CSV) that shows invoice lines, passback %, and credit amounts.

Attachments: I will drop the reconciliation workbook and the onboarding checklist in the HubSpot deal record (link below) and copy the templates to the DocuSign request if you want the PO wrapped. In short: if you can accelerate DataBridge onboarding, Pattern A is cleaner; otherwise we can stage with Pattern B and transition post-onboarding.

Link to onboarding checklist: https://redwood-hubspot.com/deals/HLX-2028-019/onboarding-checklist

If that all sounds right I'll mark the deal in HubSpot as "Ready for Procurement" and schedule a test invoice generation once we have VAT numbers.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Marketplace Ops — Redwood Inference
